title: What skills to put on a CV (with examples)
desc: Which skills to put on your CV, how to choose them from the job advert and how to prove them, with examples of hard and soft skills.
blocks: The skills section helps recruiters, and the software they use, check quickly that you match the job. The best skills section is short, honest and built around the advert.

Hard skills are technical and measurable: Excel, forklift licence, Python, food hygiene, bookkeeping, a foreign language. Soft skills are personal qualities: communication, teamwork, problem solving, organisation, customer service.
Read the job advert and underline the skills it asks for. Keep the ones that are true for you, using the same words, and add the ones that make you stand out. 6 to 12 skills is plenty.
A skill listed without proof is easy to ignore. Back up the most important ones in your work experience bullet points.
Handled 60+ customer calls a day and resolved 90% of issues on the first call.
Retail: till handling, stock control, visual merchandising, customer service
Warehouse: forklift licence, pick and pack, health and safety, inventory systems
Office: Microsoft 365, data entry, diary management, minute taking
Care: personal care, medication rounds, safeguarding, care plans
